newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RBNZ's Brash clarifies stance on NZ dlr, rates.
newsitem.headline: RBNZ's Brash clarifies stance on NZ dlr, rates.

text.p: Reserve Bank of New Zealand Governor Don Brash said in a news release on Wednesday that comments from the left-wing Alliance Party following a Tuesday meeting with Brash suggested he had been misunderstood.
Brash reiterated that he regarded the present mix of monetary conditions as "less than optimal, with the exchange rate too high, so that too much pressure is being exterted on export industries".
He also repeated that not enough disinflationary pressure was being exerted on the domestic economy.
"As a result I would prefer a different mix with a lower exchange rate and higher domestic interest rates, and I told the Alliance caucus that," Brash said.
"However, it is totally misleading to suggest that I told the Alliance that the only way of easing upward pressure on the exchange rate was through recession. This I reject."
Brash said a breach below the RBNZ's 0-3 percent inflation target was regarded as seriously as a breach on the top side.
He said the rising pressure on the exchange rate would abate over time as a result of:
* either inflationary pressures within New Zealand will fall back, which will enable domestic monetary policy to be eased;
* or inflationary pressures abroad will rise, which will prompt other countries to tighten their monetary policies, thus reducing the gap between interest rates in New Zealand and those abroad;
* or increasing concerns about the balance of payments deficit will see capital inflows into New Zealand diminish.
On Tuesday Alliance Party leader Jim Anderton said that Brash had told his party in a briefing that private sector adjustments were the order of the day.
"If you interpret that language. It means recession," Anderton said.
